clue.text: Separate lives led by king and consort ultimately becoming performer

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Rex)
separate as an adjective means apart
lives as a verb means exists, is

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word consort

explanation.surface: A royal couple living apart, the consort eventually going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by king' puts R at the front; 'ultimately' takes the T that ends consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap artist is a type of musical performer, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Girl climbed frames close to gladioli

indicators.note: frames says one piece goes around another like a picture frame

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, meaning climbed

indicators.note: close to points to the last letter of the word gladioli

explanation.surface: A girl climbing up to a frame of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Star training lawyer — Times man — after getting narrowly beaten

parts.note: a pip is the star on an army officer's shoulder
PE is physical education, training
DA is a district attorney, a US lawyer
T is short for time, so times plural gives two of them
he is a man
post is Latin for after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A star trains a lawyer and a newspaper man, then loses by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' gives T twice, one T per time; the newspaper suggestion is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pipped at the post is to be beaten at the very last moment, by a small margin.

clue.text: Diverted article leaving bottom exposed

indicators.note: leaving says the named piece departs from the word

parts.note: the rear is one's bottom
A is the indefinite article
to be outed is to be exposed publicly

explanation.surface: A piece in which someone's backside is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes A out of REAR to give RER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rerouted means sent by a different way, as traffic is diverted.

clue.text: Isolated part of UK where satellite not available

parts.note: Io is one of the moons, or satellites, of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A remote corner of Britain without satellite reception.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island in the Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a remote small island of the Inner Hebrides, so an isolated part of Britain.

clue.text: Novel that's one tenth fancy and two thirds killing picked up

indicators.note: fancy here is an adjective meaning elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means read upwards, from bottom to top
two thirds of the word survives, so its final third is dropped

parts.note: a killing is a murder

explanation.surface: A novel described in fractions: a little fancy and mostly murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' shuffles I + TENTH to THETIN; MURD, read upwards, is DRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Drum is a 1959 novel by Gunter Grass, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Make dark insinuations, mentioning leads on plot

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a plot of ground for flowers is a bed

indicators.note: leads are the front letters of the words insinuations and mentioning

explanation.surface: Someone darkly hinting at the main points of a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedim is to make dim, a literary verb for darkening or obscuring.

clue.text: By the grace of God, key cuts save spending money

indicators.note: cuts says the pieces slice into another word

parts.note: save as a preposition means except, but
DG is Dei gratia, Latin for by the grace of God, on British coins
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A prayerful note about cutting costs to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' is the container signal; 'save' means except, not keep money. DG appears on British coins as Dei gratia.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is a sum of money set aside for spending, an allowance.

clue.text: Hop over gate and wait

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the following piece

parts.note: a hop is a dance
gate is the number of spectators at a sports event, the attendance

explanation.surface: Jumping a fence and then waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is a sporting crowd figure, not a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance on someone is to wait on them fussily and obsequiously.

clue.text: Bodybuilder perhaps raised total mass in hygienic surroundings

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a total

indicators.note: in says the mass letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: hygienic means clean
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder lifting a huge weight in a spotless gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the total upwards in this down clue; 'in' and 'surroundings' together say the mass letter sits inside the hygienic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscleman is a man with highly developed muscles, as a bodybuilder may be.

clue.text: Policemen's excellent ambition to stop others

parts.note: super is a colloquial word for excellent

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the others are other ambitions, that is intents or aims
an ambition is an end or goal

explanation.surface: A policeman's fine aspiration is to stop other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' plugs one piece inside another; 'others' stands for other ambitions, the plural of the aim word, an unusual stretch the solver must accept.
explanation.definitionFit: Superintendents are senior police officers in British forces, a rank above chief inspector.

clue.text: Some would say his tower a sight to behold

indicators.note: some would say signals a word as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: his tower is the Eiffel Tower in Paris, so his is Eiffel

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous engineer's tower is worth seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'his' is Gustave Eiffel, so the word spoken is EIFFEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a striking or attractive sight, something well worth looking at.

clue.text: Star's left perhaps with no dream

parts.note: left is one example of a side, as opposed to right
something that is no dream is real

explanation.surface: A celebrity's departure perhaps not just a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to the stars, matching the adjectival force of the possessive.

clue.text: Cocaine user's epitaph making someone furious

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a common epitaph on gravestones
a cocaine user snorts the drug, so is a snorter

explanation.surface: The grave inscription for a drug addict angers someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link; read the answer as RIP SNORTER, a junkie's gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsnorter is something or someone wild and violent, a furious example of its kind.

clue.text: Deal with trendy policeman making potential howlers

parts.note: to deal is to trade
in means fashionable, trendy
DS stands for detective sergeant, a police rank

explanation.surface: Doing business with a fashionable detective who might cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'howlers' here means winds that howl, not blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are steady strong winds, which can howl, hence howlers in waiting.

clue.text: Obscure old poet -—- one quiet for so long

indicators.note: obscure as a verb means to blur, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An obscure old poet quiet for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' rearranges OLD POET to TOODLEP; 'so long' is a farewell, not a length of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is dated British slang for goodbye, a farewell like so long.

clue.text: Saying nothing, dropping hot fruit juice

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: shtum is slang for silent, saying nothing
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone keeping quiet while spilling a hot fruity drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stum is unfermented or partly fermented grape juice, a kind of fruit must.

clue.text: Briton most improperly appearing in survey

indicators.note: appearing in says the rearranged letters go inside another word

parts.note: to scan is to survey

indicators.note: improperly says the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A British person showing up wrongly in a poll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' rearranges the word most, and 'appearing in' puts the result inside the survey word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotsman is a native of Scotland and so one kind of Briton.

clue.text: Unknown philosophical principle employed in rotation of crop

indicators.note: in rotation says the pieces are turned round end to end

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
the Tao is the guiding principle of Taoist philosophy

explanation.surface: An obscure philosophy applied to a farmer's crop rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in rotation' reverses the whole run YTAO; 'employed' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaty means made of or relating to oats, a cereal crop.

clue.text: Shield the US once deployed around Cape

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the other piece
deployed means set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: America once sent forces to defend a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges THE US ONCE to ESCUTHEON, and 'around' wraps it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield on which a coat of arms is displayed in heraldry.

clue.text: Noblewoman's right dismissing church threats

indicators.note: dismissing says one piece throws out another and takes its place

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman

explanation.surface: A noblewoman entitled to sack the church in the face of menaces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Noblewoman's means 'has': the duchess has R in place of CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion by threats or force, so threats capture its sense.

clue.text: Is necessary for new work to turn to fiction

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the turned pieces follow

parts.note: a fiction is a lie

indicators.note: to turn says these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially in music

explanation.surface: A writer must turn a new piece into fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses new plus work, and the second 'to' attaches that run after the fiction word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lies upon you is incumbent on you, a duty that must be done.

clue.text: A barber's not gelling

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the demon barber of Fleet Street in the musical and penny dreadfuls

explanation.surface: A barber's shop where things fail to set.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional murderous barber of London's Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: People at odds are in disagreement, not getting on or working together.

clue.text: Island temperature halfway through shot up

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland

indicators.note: halfway through points to the letter in the centre of the word temperature

explanation.surface: An island's temperature midway through rising.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKYER is a cricket term for a ball hit high into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyer is a cricket shot hit steeply upwards, a mis-hit easy to catch.

clue.text: Ornament and tattoo-marks cut when couples go out regularly

indicators.note: dropping every two letters in turn keeps just every third letter of the words

explanation.surface: A body ornament and some tattoo marks trimmed in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove letters in pairs and keep the next: taTtoO-maRks Cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a metal neck ring worn as an ornament by ancient Celts.

clue.text: The rhino to stop being an endangered species?

definitions.text: The rhino to stop being an endangered species?

parts.words: The rhino to stop being an endangered species?
parts.note: rhino is old slang for money; cash paid so as not to be harmed by gangsters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about wildlife conservation; 'rhino' is slang for money, paid to stay safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection money is cash extorted by criminals in return for sparing the payer from harm.

clue.text: Recalled Spanish tap-dancer's entertaining ways

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Remembering how a Spanish tap-dancer used to amuse audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of tap-dancer's stands for 'has', saying the letters are held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths are ways or routes, here ones that entertain or carry a person along.

clue.text: Foreign Eurocrat around noon, entertaining his relations!

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the other piece
foreign suggests the letters are made strange, put into a new order

explanation.surface: An overseas EU official at midday amusing his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' are tales related, not family members; 'Foreign' shuffles EUROCRAT, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of stories, whose narrations amuse listeners.
